{"grade": 6, "complete": true, "main_gap": "none of substance; the lower bound of the refinement lemma asserts a false graph-theoretic claim (fewer edges than vertices ⇒ acyclic), though only the existence of one tree component is needed and follows from the same count.", "errors": [{"description": "A multigraph with fewer edges than vertices can still contain a cycle (e.g. a triangle plus isolated vertices), so 'every component is a tree' is false, and 'the component containing a_q' need not be a tree. The argument only needs some component with e_C = v_C - 1, which does follow from the edge count; the fix is one line, but as written the claim is incorrect.", "quote": "Having fewer edges than vertices, the graph contains
no cycle and no loop, since a cycle or a loop on \(v\) vertices already uses at
least \(v\) edges; hence every connected component \(C\) has \(e_C=v_C-1\) and
is a tree (an isolated vertex counts as a tree). We use the component
containing the vertex of \(a_q\)."}], "notes": "Correct answer with a genuinely complete architecture: drafting-value lemma (verified algebra), exact refinement lemma (tree-component signed sum for the lower bound; overlay construction with cut count ≤ q-1 for the upper bound), pigeonhole on 2^q subset sums, and powers-of-two construction. Sections 5-6 are extraneous. One point off for the false acyclicity claim."}
